sources: AllMusic 5/5 ("one of the greatest debuts") | RS 500 #232 (2003) #287 (2020) | Larkin Top 1000 #267 | 1001 Albums | Record Mirror 2/5 (1965) | US #6, UK #7; title single #1 US/UK | mainstream: Columbia, Melcher, session players on the title track, but the band's own folk-rock invention

Pitchfork 9.7 (Legacy Edition, 2003) | Rolling Stone 500 (2003) entry: 'set the stage for country rock' | Rolling Stone 1968 (Barry Gifford): lukewarm, 'an interesting album' | Toledo Blade (Rod Lockwood, 2003): 'seminal', 'never a big seller' | American Songwriter (Jim Beviglia, 2025): 'considered a flop at the time' | mainstream: genre turn against the band's rock audience, mostly covers with Nashville session players

Ultimate Classic Rock (Frank Mastropolo, 2016): Billboard No. 24 https://ultimateclassicrock.com/the-byrds-fifth-dimension/ | Classic Rock Review (2021): 'highly influential', 'less commercially successful than its 1965 predecessors' https://classicrockreview.com/?p=19841 | Psychedelic Sight (2012): 'seminal psychedelic album' but 'a good bit... surrendered to filler' https://psychedelicsight.com/fifth-dimension-byrds/ | Head Heritage (2004): 'certainly inconsistent' | importance: transitional record after Gene Clark left | mainstream: Columbia house producer, folk covers beside band-written experiments
